1	/**
2	 * Bulk-import a real mod.io catalogue into `GameMod` for NxLabs Phase 3 — the
3	 * mod.io counterpart to `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts` and
4	 * `scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts`. Same shape, same safety rails,
5	 * same idempotency guarantee. Read those two first if you haven't; this one
6	 * only documents where mod.io's real API and data shape force a different
7	 * approach.
8	 *
9	 * GAMES COVERED (checked live 2026-09-20 against mod.io's own `/v1/games`
10	 * listing, matched by name to lib/games.ts's GAME_FAMILIES — these 4 were
11	 * confirmed to have a real, active mod.io presence; nothing here is guessed):
12	 *   mod.io game id 5289 → "Core Keeper"            → gameFamily "corekeeper"
13	 *   mod.io game id  264 → "Space Engineers"         → gameFamily "spaceengineers"
14	 *   mod.io game id  254 → "Insurgency: Sandstorm"   → gameFamily "sandstorm"
15	 *   mod.io game id  169 → "MORDHAU"                 → gameFamily "mordhau"
16	 *
17	 * SOURCE: mod.io REST API v1, https://docs.mod.io/restapiref/ — the real
18	 * developer-account `MODIO_API_KEY` now in `.env` (confirmed live against
19	 * `GET /v1/games`, see below). One endpoint does all the work here:
20	 * `GET /v1/games/{game-id}/mods` already returns the FULL mod object (logo,
21	 * media.images[], stats, tags, submitted_by) in one call — unlike Modrinth,
22	 * there is no separate "search hit" vs "full project" split and no bulk
23	 * `?ids=[...]` follow-up call needed. Paged with `_limit`/`_offset`, real
24	 * `result_total` in every response.
25	 *
26	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
27	 * RATE LIMIT (checked live, NOT assumed from earlier per-game-key research)
28	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29	 * The response to `GET /v1/games` carries `x-modio-key: user` — mod.io's own
30	 * header naming this a USER-linked (general developer account) key, not a
31	 * GAME-linked one. mod.io's docs (checked live 2026-09-20) are explicit that
32	 * the "unlimited requests" tier only applies to game-linked keys; a
33	 * user-linked key like this one is documented at 60 requests/minute. No
34	 * `X-RateLimit-*` headers are returned at all (mod.io deprecated them
35	 * platform-wide in Nov 2022 in favor of a `retry-after` header on actual 429s
36	 * — confirmed absent on every real response this script's development burst-
37	 * tested, including 60 requests fired in ~26s with zero throttling observed).
38	 * Since the documented ceiling (60/min) is the only real number to plan
39	 * around, this script self-paces under it — see RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN — and
40	 * retries 429s honoring `Retry-After`, same pattern as the Modrinth script.
41	 *
42	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
43	 * LEGAL / FETCH-AT-INSTALL-ONLY (verified live, not assumed)
44	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	 * Checked the full shape of a real mod object (Core Keeper's top-downloaded
46	 * mod, "CoreLib") field by field: there is no `license` key anywhere in the
47	 * response, at any nesting level. mod.io's API has no per-mod license concept
48	 * at all (unlike Modrinth's `license.id`). Consequences, matching this
49	 * repo's established Thunderstore/Steam Workshop precedent for sources with
50	 * no license field:
51	 *   - `license` is always written as `null`. Never fabricate one.
52	 *   - This script NEVER downloads/mirrors/rehosts an actual mod file. It
53	 *     stores metadata + the real hotlinked mod.io CDN image URLs
54	 *     (`image.modcdn.io`/`thumb.modcdn.io`) only — `logo` and
55	 *     `media.images[]` are legitimately part of the public API response, not
56	 *     scraped. The real file stays fetched at INSTALL TIME by the worker,
57	 *     exactly like every other source; this script performs zero mod-file
58	 *     downloads, only catalogue JSON.
59	 *
60	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
61	 * SPACE ENGINEERS NEEDS A CONTENT-TYPE FILTER MODRINTH-STYLE (verified live)
62	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
63	 * mod.io's Space Engineers catalogue is huge (165,922 listed items) but the
64	 * overwhelming majority is NOT server-installable mod content:
65	 *   tags=Blueprint  → 144,710 (87%) — personal ship/rover designs, subscribed
66	 *                     per-player in-game; nothing a dedicated server installs.
67	 *   tags=World      →  16,945       — full save-game worlds, not mods.
68	 *   tags=ingameScript →    744      — Programmable Block scripts a player
69	 *                     pastes into their own grid; not a server-side file.
70	 *   tags=scenario   →      37       — custom scenario templates.
71	 *   tags=Mod        →   3,113       — actual code/content mods, loaded via
72	 *                     the game's real `Mods=` list — this is the one bucket
73	 *                     that is genuinely "install this on my dedicated server"
74	 *                     content, the SE analogue of Modrinth's `environment`
75	 *                     facet excluding client-only content. THIS script only
76	 *                     imports `tags=Mod` for Space Engineers. Core Keeper,
77	 *                     Sandstorm, and Mordhau have no comparable non-installable
78	 *                     bucket in their own tag taxonomies (checked live, see
79	 *                     CATEGORY_GROUP below) so no equivalent filter applies
80	 *                     to them — matches Modrinth's own principle of only
81	 *                     filtering where the source draws a real distinction,
82	 *                     never inventing one.
83	 *
84	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
85	 * CATEGORY (verified live per game — mod.io has no Modrinth-style structural
86	 * `project_type`, so the closest real per-mod facet is each game's own
87	 * checkbox/dropdown tag taxonomy, which differs completely per game)
88	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	 * `GET /v1/games/{id}/tags` was checked live for all 4 games. One tag group
90	 * per game is the real "what kind of content is this" facet; the rest
91	 * (Game Version, Grid Size, Safety, Theme, Time, Setting, ...) are not.
92	 *   corekeeper (5289): group "Type" — Visual/Audio/Item/NPC/Quality of Life/
93	 *     Overhaul/Language/Library.
94	 *   spaceengineers (264): every imported row is already tags=Mod (see above),
95	 *     so category is trivially "Mod" — no group lookup needed.
96	 *   sandstorm (254): group "Mods" — Total Conversion/Custom Theater/Game
97	 *     Mode/Mutator. A row with no tag from this group (i.e. a map with no
98	 *     mod-type tag) falls back to the game's own `ugc_name` ("Mods") —
99	 *     Sandstorm draws no client/server distinction between its "Maps" and
100	 *     "Mods" tag groups (a map is exactly as server-installable as a mod;
101	 *     dedicated servers rotate maps), so both are kept, only the label
102	 *     differs.
103	 *   mordhau (169): group "Type" — Map/Skin/Serverside Only/Dependency/Admin
104	 *     Tool/Item Removal/RCON/Audio.
105	 * A mod with none of its own tags present in the game's category group falls
106	 * back to that game's real `ugc_name` from `/v1/games` (Core Keeper "Mods",
107	 * Sandstorm "Mods", Mordhau "Mods") — never a fabricated label.
108	 *
109	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
110	 * QUALITY GATE (documented, not guessed)
111	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
112	 * downloads_total > 1000 (DEFAULT_MIN_DOWNLOADS) — the SAME numeric floor
113	 * import-modrinth-catalog.ts uses, applied AFTER the Space Engineers
114	 * tags=Mod filter above. Checked live where this floor lands for each real
115	 * pool: corekeeper ~180/312, spaceengineers(Mod) ~1050/3113, sandstorm
116	 * ~410/773, mordhau ~700/1435 — a real, meaningful cut in every case, not
117	 * a no-op and not a catalogue-gutting one.
118	 *   Tried Modrinth's disjoint second pass (subscribers_total as the
119	 *   follows-analogue) before deciding against it, same as
120	 *   import-thunderstore-catalog.ts's documented rating_score finding:
121	 *   checked live how many rows would clear subscribers_total>50 AND
122	 *   downloads_total<=1000 (i.e. what a second pass would actually add) for
123	 *   every one of the 4 games — corekeeper 0, sandstorm 0, mordhau 1,
124	 *   spaceengineers(Mod) 0. Not a real disjoint gain anywhere. Documenting the
125	 *   finding here instead of shipping a provably-near-dead code path.
126	 * Pagination requests `_sort=-downloads_total` and stops each game's pass the
127	 * moment a page's last row is at or under the floor — real early-stop, not a
128	 * full scan of large pools (matters most for Space Engineers's 3,113-row
129	 * tags=Mod pool).
130	 *
131	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
132	 * IDENTITY / SLUG STRATEGY (matches import-github-catalog.ts's pattern, not
133	 * Modrinth's plain slug-is-the-key one)
134	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
135	 * mod.io's real immutable identity is the numeric mod `id` — its `name_id`
136	 * (kebab slug) CAN be changed by the author later (mod.io lets creators edit
137	 * their profile URL). So: match existing rows by (gameFamily, source:
138	 * "mod_io", sourceId: String(id)) FIRST. Found → update in place, `slug`
139	 * never touched. Not found → create with slug = mod's own `name_id`
140	 * (de-duplicated against every slug already used in that gameFamily —
141	 * collision is possible in principle even though mod.io enforces per-game
142	 * uniqueness of name_id, because this repo's uniqueness is per-gameFamily,
143	 * which is a 1:1 mapping here anyway, so in practice collisions shouldn't
144	 * occur, but the check costs one query and costs nothing if it never fires).
145	 * The actual write is still `db.gameMod.upsert`/`create`/`update` — same
146	 * `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` constraint as every other importer.
147	 *
148	 * FIELD NOTES:
149	 *   - `description` = mod.io's `summary` (short tagline, matches Modrinth's
150	 *     `description` field length/role).
151	 *   - `longDescription` = mod.io's `description_plaintext` (the real full
152	 *     project-page body, HTML tags already stripped by mod.io itself) — only
153	 *     written when non-empty, same "real longer body or null, never a copy
154	 *     of the short one" rule GameMod.longDescription's schema doc states.
155	 *   - `iconUrl` = `logo.thumb_320x180`. mod.io has no separate small square
156	 *     icon field the way Modrinth does — the "logo" IS the primary image,
157	 *     always a 16:9 banner. Using the smallest real thumbnail mod.io itself
158	 *     generates, not a made-up crop.
159	 *   - `galleryUrls` = `media.images[].original`, capped at GALLERY_CAP,
160	 *     in the API's own returned order. mod.io does not publish a
161	 *     featured/ordering flag on images the way Modrinth's gallery does, so
162	 *     unlike the Modrinth script there is nothing to sort by — this is
163	 *     documented, not a missed field.
164	 *   - `authorName`/`authorAvatarUrl` = `submitted_by.username` /
165	 *     `submitted_by.avatar.thumb_100x100`, real fields already present on
166	 *     every mod object (no separate user-lookup call needed, unlike
167	 *     Modrinth's bulk `/users?ids=` step).
168	 *   - `gameVersions` = every one of the mod's own tags that matches that
169	 *     game's real "Game Version" tag group (present for Core Keeper only,
170	 *     checked live — the other 3 games' tag taxonomies have no version
171	 *     group at all, so this is `[]` for them, matching the schema's own
172	 *     "empty = the source has no version list, not the same as none" rule).
173	 *   - `loaders` = `[]` always. mod.io has no loader/platform-manager concept
174	 *     analogous to Modrinth's `loaders` for any of these 4 games.
175	 *   - `serverSide` = derived from Core Keeper's real "Application Type"
176	 *     checkbox group (Client/Server — the one game of the 4 whose taxonomy
177	 *     draws this distinction at all, checked live): "Server" tag present →
178	 *     "required"; "Client" present without "Server" → "unsupported"; neither
179	 *     → null (unknown, kept rather than guessed, same as Modrinth's own
180	 *     null-when-unknown convention). Always null for the other 3 games —
181	 *     verified live they have no such field.
182	 *
183	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
184	 * KNOWN GAP, DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN SILENTLY LEFT (not this script's job)
185	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
186	 * Checked `lib/mod-install-support.ts`: none of corekeeper/spaceengineers/
187	 * sandstorm/mordhau are in `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES` today, so these rows will
188	 * all render "install it yourself in Files" regardless of source — the same
189	 * documented degrade every not-yet-wired family already gets. Since the
190	 * family gate fails before the source gate is ever checked, adding "mod_io"
191	 * to `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES` would currently have ZERO visible effect for any
192	 * of these 4 families and was deliberately NOT done in this pass — it is
193	 * real, separate, future work (writing each game's real config-write
194	 * mechanism — Space Engineers/Core Keeper/Mordhau/Sandstorm dedicated
195	 * servers each have their own way of taking a mod.io id, none of them
196	 * researched yet) that a pure catalogue-population pass should not bundle in
197	 * without deploying and verifying the mechanism for real.
198	 *
199	 * SAFETY: same as every other writing script in this repo — dry run by
200	 * default, `scripts/db-target-guard.ts` enforces NXEON_DB_TARGET.
201	 *
202	 *   Dry run, one small game first:
203	 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx scripts/import-modio-catalog.ts \
204	 *       --games=corekeeper
205	 *
206	 *   Real write, same slice:
207	 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx scripts/import-modio-catalog.ts \
208	 *       --games=corekeeper --apply
209	 *
210	 *   Full real run (all 4 games, default threshold):
211	 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon npx tsx scripts/import-modio-catalog.ts --apply
212	 */
213	
214	import { assertDbTarget } from "./db-target-guard";
215	assertDbTarget("import-modio-catalog.ts");
216	
217	import { db } from "../lib/db";
218	import type { GameFamily } from "../lib/games";
219	
220	const UA = "Nxeon/1.0 (mods@nxeon.cloud)";
221	const MODIO_KEY = process.env.MODIO_API_KEY ?? "";
222	const API = "https://api.mod.io/v1";
223	
224	if (!MODIO_KEY) {
225	  console.error("Refusing to run: MODIO_API_KEY is not set. Nothing was written.");
226	  process.exit(1);
227	}
228	
229	// ── Tunable script constants ─────────────────────────────────────────────
230	const DEFAULT_MIN_DOWNLOADS = 1000; // same floor as import-modrinth-catalog.ts, see file header
231	const DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN = 50; // conservative margin under mod.io's documented 60/min for user-linked keys
232	const PAGE_SIZE = 100;
233	const GALLERY_CAP = 8; // matches the Modrinth/verify-gamemods.ts convention
234	
235	const ALL_GAMES = ["corekeeper", "spaceengineers", "sandstorm", "mordhau"] as const;
236	type Game = (typeof ALL_GAMES)[number];
237	
238	const GAME_TO_FAMILY: Record<Game, GameFamily> = {
239	  corekeeper: "corekeeper",
240	  spaceengineers: "spaceengineers",
241	  sandstorm: "sandstorm",
242	  mordhau: "mordhau",
243	};
244	
245	/** Real mod.io game ids — see file header for how these were confirmed live. */
246	const GAME_ID: Record<Game, number> = {
247	  corekeeper: 5289,
248	  spaceengineers: 264,
249	  sandstorm: 254,
250	  mordhau: 169,
251	};
252	
253	/** Server-relevant content-type filter — see file header. Only Space
254	 *  Engineers' taxonomy has a real non-installable majority bucket to exclude. */
255	const TAGS_FILTER: Partial<Record<Game, string>> = {
256	  spaceengineers: "Mod",
257	};
258	
259	/** Which live tag group is "the" category facet for each game — see file header. */
260	const CATEGORY_GROUP: Partial<Record<Game, string>> = {
261	  corekeeper: "Type",
262	  sandstorm: "Mods",
263	  mordhau: "Type",
264	};
265	
266	/** Only Core Keeper's taxonomy draws a real client/server distinction. */
267	const APPLICATION_TYPE_GROUP: Partial<Record<Game, string>> = {
268	  corekeeper: "Application Type",
269	};
270	
271	/** Only Core Keeper's taxonomy has a real game-version group. */
272	const GAME_VERSION_GROUP: Partial<Record<Game, string>> = {
273	  corekeeper: "Game Version",
274	};
275	
276	// ── CLI args ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
277	function parseArgs(argv: string[]) {
278	  const get = (name: string) => argv.find((a) => a.startsWith(`--${name}=`))?.split("=").slice(1).join("=");
279	  const gamesArg = get("games");
280	  const games = (gamesArg ? gamesArg.split(",") : [...ALL_GAMES]).filter((g): g is Game =>
281	    (ALL_GAMES as readonly string[]).includes(g)
282	  );
283	  return {
284	    apply: argv.includes("--apply"),
285	    minDownloads: Number(get("min-downloads") ?? DEFAULT_MIN_DOWNLOADS),
286	    ratePerMin: Number(get("rate-per-min") ?? DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN),
287	    maxPages: get("max-pages") ? Number(get("max-pages")) : undefined, // smoke-test cap, not a real-run knob
288	    games: games.length ? games : [...ALL_GAMES],
289	  };
290	}
291	
292	// ── Rate-limited, retrying fetch (same pattern as import-modrinth-catalog.ts) ──
293	class RateLimiter {
294	  private minIntervalMs: number;
295	  private last = 0;
296	  constructor(perMin: number) {
297	    this.minIntervalMs = 60_000 / perMin;
298	  }
299	  async wait() {
300	    const now = Date.now();
301	    const elapsed = now - this.last;
302	    if (elapsed < this.minIntervalMs) {
303	      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, this.minIntervalMs - elapsed));
304	    }
305	    this.last = Date.now();
306	  }
307	}
308	
309	async function apiFetch(limiter: RateLimiter, url: string, attempt = 1): Promise<Response> {
310	  await limiter.wait();
311	  const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { "User-Agent": UA } });
312	  if (res.status === 429 && attempt <= 6) {
313	    const retryAfterHeader = res.headers.get("retry-after");
314	    const retryAfterMs = retryAfterHeader ? Number(retryAfterHeader) * 1000 : 0;
315	    const backoffMs = Math.max(retryAfterMs, 1000 * 2 ** attempt);
316	    console.warn(`  [rate-limit] 429 on ${url} — backing off ${Math.round(backoffMs / 1000)}s (attempt ${attempt})`);
317	    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, backoffMs));
318	    return apiFetch(limiter, url, attempt + 1);
319	  }
320	  if (res.status >= 500 && attempt <= 4) {
321	    const backoffMs = 1000 * 2 ** attempt;
322	    console.warn(`  [server-error] ${res.status} on ${url} — retrying in ${Math.round(backoffMs / 1000)}s`);
323	    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, backoffMs));
324	    return apiFetch(limiter, url, attempt + 1);
325	  }
326	  return res;
327	}
328	
329	// ── mod.io types (only the fields we read) ───────────────────────────────
330	type ModioImage = { filename: string; original: string; thumb_320x180?: string; thumb_1280x720?: string };
331	type ModioTag = { name: string; name_localized?: string; date_added?: number };
332	type ModioUser = {
333	  username: string;
334	  display_name_portal?: string | null;
335	  avatar?: { original?: string; thumb_100x100?: string } | null;
336	};
337	type ModioMod = {
338	  id: number;
339	  name: string;
340	  name_id: string;
341	  summary: string;
342	  description_plaintext?: string | null;
343	  profile_url: string;
344	  logo?: ModioImage | null;
345	  media?: { images?: ModioImage[] };
346	  tags?: ModioTag[];
347	  stats: { downloads_total: number; subscribers_total: number };
348	  submitted_by: ModioUser;
349	};
350	type ModioModsResponse = { data: ModioMod[]; result_total: number };
351	type ModioGame = { id: number; name: string; name_id: string; ugc_name: string };
352	type ModioTagGroup = { name: string; type: string; tags: string[] };
353	type ModioTagsResponse = { data: ModioTagGroup[] };
354	
355	async function fetchGame(limiter: RateLimiter, gameId: number): Promise<ModioGame> {
356	  const res = await apiFetch(limiter, `${API}/games/${gameId}?api_key=${MODIO_KEY}`);
357	  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`mod.io returned HTTP ${res.status} fetching game ${gameId}`);
358	  return (await res.json()) as ModioGame;
359	}
360	
361	async function fetchTagGroups(limiter: RateLimiter, gameId: number): Promise<ModioTagGroup[]> {
362	  const res = await apiFetch(limiter, `${API}/games/${gameId}/tags?api_key=${MODIO_KEY}`);
363	  if (!res.ok) return [];
364	  const body = (await res.json()) as ModioTagsResponse;
365	  return body.data;
366	}
367	
368	function galleryUrlsFrom(images: ModioImage[] | undefined): string[] {
369	  return (images ?? []).slice(0, GALLERY_CAP).map((img) => img.original);
370	}
371	
372	function categoryFor(mod: ModioMod, game: Game, ugcName: string, groupValues: Set<string>): string {
373	  const groupName = CATEGORY_GROUP[game];
374	  if (groupName) {
375	    const hit = (mod.tags ?? []).find((t) => groupValues.has(t.name));
376	    if (hit) return hit.name;
377	  }
378	  return ugcName;
379	}
380	
381	function gameVersionsFor(mod: ModioMod, game: Game, versionValues: Set<string>): string[] {
382	  if (!GAME_VERSION_GROUP[game]) return [];
383	  return (mod.tags ?? []).filter((t) => versionValues.has(t.name)).map((t) => t.name);
384	}
385	
386	function serverSideFor(mod: ModioMod, game: Game, appTypeValues: Set<string>): string | null {
387	  if (!APPLICATION_TYPE_GROUP[game]) return null;
388	  const tagNames = new Set((mod.tags ?? []).filter((t) => appTypeValues.has(t.name)).map((t) => t.name));
389	  if (tagNames.has("Server")) return "required";
390	  if (tagNames.has("Client")) return "unsupported";
391	  return null;
392	}
393	
394	type Counters = { fetched: number; belowFloor: number; eligible: number; upserted: number; created: number; updated: number; skipped: number; failed: number };
395	function emptyCounters(): Counters {
396	  return { fetched: 0, belowFloor: 0, eligible: 0, upserted: 0, created: 0, updated: 0, skipped: 0, failed: 0 };
397	}
398	
399	async function importGame(opts: {
400	  game: Game;
401	  limiter: RateLimiter;
402	  apply: boolean;
403	  minDownloads: number;
404	  maxPages?: number;
405	}) {
406	  const { game, limiter, apply, minDownloads, maxPages } = opts;
407	  const gameFamily = GAME_TO_FAMILY[game];
408	  const gameId = GAME_ID[game];
409	  const counters = emptyCounters();
410	
411	  console.log(`\n=== ${game} (mod.io game id ${gameId}) → gameFamily "${gameFamily}" ===`);
412	
413	  const [gameInfo, tagGroups] = await Promise.all([fetchGame(limiter, gameId), fetchTagGroups(limiter, gameId)]);
414	  const groupTagValues = (name: string | undefined): Set<string> =>
415	    new Set(tagGroups.find((g) => g.name === name)?.tags ?? []);
416	  const categoryValues = groupTagValues(CATEGORY_GROUP[game]);
417	  const versionValues = groupTagValues(GAME_VERSION_GROUP[game]);
418	  const appTypeValues = groupTagValues(APPLICATION_TYPE_GROUP[game]);
419	
420	  // Preload every existing mod_io row for this family — sourceId → existing
421	  // slug (never re-slugify on update), plus every slug already in use for
422	  // create-time collision avoidance. See file header's IDENTITY section.
423	  const existingRows = await db.gameMod.findMany({
424	    where: { gameFamily, source: "mod_io" },
425	    select: { id: true, slug: true, sourceId: true },
426	  });
427	  const existingBySourceId = new Map(existingRows.filter((r) => r.sourceId).map((r) => [r.sourceId as string, r]));
428	  const usedSlugs = new Set(existingRows.map((r) => r.slug));
429	  console.log(`  ${existingRows.length} existing mod_io row(s) already in this family`);
430	
431	  const tagsFilter = TAGS_FILTER[game];
432	  let offset = 0;
433	  let page = 0;
434	  for (;;) {
435	    if (maxPages !== undefined && page >= maxPages) break;
436	    const tagsParam = tagsFilter ? `&tags=${encodeURIComponent(tagsFilter)}` : "";
437	    const url = `${API}/games/${gameId}/mods?api_key=${MODIO_KEY}&_limit=${PAGE_SIZE}&_offset=${offset}&_sort=-downloads_total${tagsParam}`;
438	    const res = await apiFetch(limiter, url);
439	    if (!res.ok) {
440	      console.error(`  [list] offset=${offset} → HTTP ${res.status}, stopping this game's pass early`);
441	      break;
442	    }
443	    const body = (await res.json()) as ModioModsResponse;
444	    page++;
445	    counters.fetched += body.data.length;
446	    if (body.data.length === 0) break;
447	
448	    const eligible = body.data.filter((m) => m.stats.downloads_total > minDownloads);
449	    counters.belowFloor += body.data.length - eligible.length;
450	    counters.eligible += eligible.length;
451	
452	    for (const mod of eligible) {
453	      if (!mod.name_id) {
454	        counters.skipped++;
455	        continue;
456	      }
457	      const category = categoryFor(mod, game, gameInfo.ugc_name, categoryValues);
458	      const data = {
459	        name: mod.name,
460	        category,
461	        description: mod.summary || null,
462	        longDescription: mod.description_plaintext || null,
463	        iconUrl: mod.logo?.thumb_320x180 ?? mod.logo?.original ?? null,
464	        url: mod.profile_url,
465	        downloads: mod.stats.downloads_total,
466	        license: null,
467	        gameVersions: gameVersionsFor(mod, game, versionValues),
468	        loaders: [] as string[],
469	        serverSide: serverSideFor(mod, game, appTypeValues),
470	        galleryUrls: galleryUrlsFrom(mod.media?.images),
471	        authorName: mod.submitted_by.display_name_portal || mod.submitted_by.username || null,
472	        authorAvatarUrl: mod.submitted_by.avatar?.thumb_100x100 ?? mod.submitted_by.avatar?.original ?? null,
473	        source: "mod_io",
474	        sourceId: String(mod.id),
475	        active: true,
476	        verifiedAt: new Date(),
477	        upstreamOk: true,
478	        upstreamNote: null as string | null,
479	      };
480	
481	      if (!apply) {
482	        counters.upserted++;
483	        continue;
484	      }
485	
486	      const existing = existingBySourceId.get(String(mod.id));
487	      try {
488	        if (existing) {
489	          await db.gameMod.update({ where: { id: existing.id }, data });
490	          counters.updated++;
491	        } else {
492	          let slug = mod.name_id;
493	          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3 && usedSlugs.has(slug); attempt++) {
494	            slug = attempt === 0 ? `${mod.name_id}-${mod.id}` : `${mod.name_id}-${mod.id}-${attempt}`;
495	          }
496	          usedSlugs.add(slug);
497	          await db.gameMod.create({ data: { gameFamily, slug, ...data } });
498	          counters.created++;
499	        }
500	        counters.upserted++;
501	      } catch (e) {
502	        counters.failed++;
503	        const msg = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
504	        console.error(`  [db] failed to upsert ${game}/${mod.name_id}: ${msg}`);
505	      }
506	    }
507	
508	    console.log(
509	      `  [${game}] page=${page} offset=${offset} fetched=${body.data.length} eligible=${eligible.length} total_hits=${body.result_total} ` +
510	        `(running: fetched=${counters.fetched} eligible=${counters.eligible} upserted=${counters.upserted} created=${counters.created} updated=${counters.updated} skipped=${counters.skipped} failed=${counters.failed})`
511	    );
512	
513	    // Real early-stop: rows are sorted by -downloads_total, so once a page's
514	    // last (lowest-downloads) row is at or under the floor, every remaining
515	    // page is too — matters most for spaceengineers's 3,113-row tags=Mod pool.
516	    const lastRow = body.data[body.data.length - 1];
517	    if (lastRow && lastRow.stats.downloads_total <= minDownloads) break;
518	
519	    offset += PAGE_SIZE;
520	    if (offset >= body.result_total) break;
521	  }
522	
523	  return counters;
524	}

527	  const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
528	  console.log(

531	      `rate: ${args.ratePerMin}/min${args.maxPages ? `; max-pages=${args.maxPages} (smoke test)` : ""}`
532	  );

540	    perGame[game] = counters;
541	    for (const k of Object.keys(totals) as (keyof Counters)[]) totals[k] += counters[k];
542	    console.log(

544	    );
545	  }
546	
547	  console.log(`\n============================================================`);
548	  console.log(`FINAL SUMMARY (${args.apply ? "APPLIED" : "DRY RUN — nothing written"})`);
549	  for (const game of args.games) {

551	    console.log(
552	      `  ${game.padEnd(16)} fetched=${c.fetched.toString().padStart(6)} eligible=${c.eligible.toString().padStart(6)} created=${c.created.toString().padStart(6)} updated=${c.updated.toString().padStart(6)} skipped=${c.skipped} failed=${c.failed}`
553	    );

557	  );
558	}

87:- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
88:- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
97:- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.

content.thinking:
Now I have a solid, verified list of well-known repos: ReHLDS, ReAPI, ReGameDLL_CS, ReUnion, ReVoice, plus the ReDeathmatch_AMXX gameplay mod, each with real star counts confirming their popularity.

I also found PluginyCS/BasePack, a curated Linux base plugin pack for CS 1.6 servers, and the popular Zombie-Escape gamemode — together forming the recognized "rehlds org" ecosystem that dominates modern CS 1.6 Linux server hosting, which matches what I already knew and is now empirically confirmed. I'll start seeding CS16 into prisma/seed-gamemods.ts, listing ReHLDS as the core engine replacement sourced from GitHub.

ReGameDLL_CS, ReAPI, AMX Mod X, ReUnion, ReVoice, the BasePack, ReDeathmatch, and Zombie-Escape round out a solid list of nine verified entries — honest rather than padded. Now it's time to set up the worktree and start writing the actual implementation code.

I'm planning the concrete deliverables for adding new Steam Workshop appids, starting by editing the FAMILY_APPID config to add entries for GMod, Space Engineers, Barotrauma, Terraria (using the "terraria" key since tModLoader is just Terraria's modding platform), Stationeers, and Killing Floor 2, working through each game family's correct appid mapping.

Necesse gets appid 1169040, Conan Exiles uses family key "conan" (not "conanexiles") with appid 440900, and I'm adding DayZ as a new family entry since it's one of the five newly-added games needing wire mods. I also need to add CS2 with appid 730 since the task explicitly mentions "CS2 maps" even though CS2 isn't currently in the existing family list.

For the Steam Workshop importer, I'm confirming CS2 (730) should be included since workshop maps are common for community servers, even though CS2 already has extensive plugin support via GitHub sources like Metamod and CSS. I'm deliberately excluding Arma Reforger (verified not a real Steam Workshop target), ETS2/ATS (real Workshop items exist but no server-side mod concept applies), and CS:GO 1.6 (predates Workshop entirely, so I'll stick with the AMXX/GitHub approach for that one instead).

I'm finalizing the list of ten new appids to add to FAMILY_APPID: GMod, Space Engineers, Barotrauma, Terraria, Stationeers, Killing Floor 2, Necesse, Conan Exiles, DayZ, and CS2. This doubles the existing config from ten entries to twenty, which is exactly the minimal, additive change requested — I'm avoiding touching any internals of the shared import script since another agent is working on it concurrently, limiting myself to just the config addition and a header comment update.

There's some risk of merge conflict, but it's documented as expected and acceptable per the task's instructions, so I'll proceed.

For the new Vintage Story ModDB importer, I need to check the API response shape more closely—the side field, category/tags, download URL pattern—and look for a per-mod detail endpoint covering description, downloads, license, and changelog. The list endpoint already gives modid, assetid, downloads, follows, trendingpoints, comments, name, summary, modidstrs, author, urlalias, side, type, logo, tags, and lastreleased.

I want to sample a few entries to verify exact values for the side field (server/client/both), and check whether there's a per-mod detail endpoint like /api/mod/{id} for the fuller description.

For the new Factorio Mod Portal importer, since it's metadata/listing only with no download proxy, I'll use /api/mods (paged) plus /api/mods/{name}/full for descriptions. The listing gives name, title, owner, summary, downloads_count, category, score, and latest_release, so I should fetch the full endpoint for a real mod to see what additional fields like description, releases, and tags look like.

I need to find an actual popular mod name rather than a placeholder junk entry — something like a well-known mod — so I'll query sorted by downloads_count to find a genuinely popular one and fetch its full record.

For the mod.io Eco addition, I need Eco's game id; the earlier search attempt likely failed due to an empty MODIO_KEY from an extraction/quoting issue, similar to what happened with Steam, so I should retry the game search after verifying the key extraction is correct this time.

For ficsit.app I'm skipping it entirely due to confirmed ToS risk, with no code changes needed — just documenting that decision. On new game wiring: DayZ gets added to the Steam Workshop family via its appid, Arma Reforger's real ecosystem runs on Bohemia's own Workshop rather than Steam so building an importer for it is out of scope this pass and I'll document it honestly as future work, and CS 1.6 will get hand-seeded real AMXX/ReHLDS ecosystem repos added into the seed file's CS16 array from GitHub sources.

For ETS2/ATS, there's no real server-catalog mod ecosystem so I'm documenting that honestly rather than building an importer. I'm also checking specific missing mods — Noisium and ScalableLux need to be added to the Minecraft array with verified Modrinth slugs, while Rust's GatherManager/StackSizeController and Valheim's BetterNetworking are already correctly handled, so those are just audit findings to report. Now I'm starting to work through the 22 zero-mod games one by one to figure out which source closes each gap, starting with Bedrock edition where there isn't really a comparable mod ecosystem to draw from.

Terraria closes via Steam Workshop/tModLoader. ARK:SA and Satisfactory remain genuine gaps since their only real platforms (CurseForge, ficsit.app) are excluded per audit ToS rules. Checking 7 Days to Die next — it doesn't appear to have native Steam Workshop support historically, so I need to verify where its mods are actually distributed.

But this fix lives inside import-thunderstore-catalog.ts, which is explicitly off-limits per the coordination note, and backfill-upstream-updated.ts is tightly coupled to the other agent's concurrent mod-description-pipeline work, so touching either risks stepping on someone else's changes.

The task text explicitly carves out an exception for import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts's appid config, but there's no equivalent exception for import-thunderstore-catalog.ts — and scanning the prompt again, it doesn't actually list Thunderstore or V Rising as one of my deliverables at all.

So this resolves cleanly: the V Rising/Thunderstore item only appears in the audit's own table, which my task prompt didn't adopt — it only enumerated items 1-4 as "new suppliers to add." That work belongs to a different concurrent agent's fix, so I shouldn't touch import-thunderstore-catalog.ts at all.

Moving through the remaining gaps: enshrouded has no identified source in my task list, so I'll report it honestly as a genuine gap given how immature its modding scene still is. Factorio, gmod, and conan are all closed out via new importers or Steam Workshop appids I've added, and now I'm checking theforest against my task list.

Necesse closed via the new Steam Workshop appid 1169040 with 547 items. Nightingale might have mod.io integration worth checking live. Killing Floor 2 needs verification since I never confirmed its Workshop item total in the second batch query due to the earlier key issue.

Barotrauma is closed via the new Steam Workshop appid with 83,122 items, solidly covering the gap even without checking mod.io separately. The Isle isn't part of the requested source list, so I'll skip verifying it and just note it as out of scope. Stationeers is closed via the new Steam Workshop appid as well.

Eco can be closed through mod.io's Eco listing, though I still need to confirm its game id via search. Recounting the task's list, only 20 games are actually named despite the task referencing 22, so I expect some discrepancy that needs re-verification against the live database.

I'm also noticing that on nxeon_staging, only 10 families have non-zero counts out of the full 47-family list, meaning far more than 20 families are effectively at zero there — quite different from prod's zero-count, since prod already has 45,761 rows spread across many more populated families via the existing steamworkshop importer.

Since my work targets the safer nxeon_staging DB, I should clearly caveat in the report that my "before" numbers reflect staging's sparser state, not prod, and note that applying the same importers to prod later (via an explicit owner-run command) would close the same families there too, consistent with not pushing or deploying myself. Next I want to check mod.io for Eco and Nightingale, the KF2 Workshop total, and Abiotic Factor's mod.io presence.

I'm confirming Eco's mod.io data now: 592 mods with a "Type" tag group (Item/Object/Species/Blockset/Script/External Tool/Addon) but no server/client distinction like Core Keeper has, so serverSide stays null for Eco. Now I'm moving on to check Vintage Story's data.

Vintage Story's "side" field shows both=7003, client=868, server=813 -- I should include "both" and "server" mods (7,816 total) while excluding the 868 client-only mods, following the same principle of excluding client-only content when the source draws that distinction. I still need to figure out a sensible download-based quality floor, and I've also hit a snag where the single-mod detail endpoint returns 404 for id=1, so I need to try a real modid like 11998 instead.

Switching to Factorio, I'm checking whether the numeric endpoint uses urlalias instead. The /full endpoint gives rich metadata -- long descriptions, categories, tags, release counts, license, and source links -- so I'll map description to longDescription and summary to the short description field, with category as a single clean string. Since the task only requires metadata import and not actual downloads, I'm weighing whether I need to hit /full for every mod or if the listing endpoint's summary data is sufficient.

I'll mirror the two-phase pattern used for Modrinth (bulk list first, then fetch full details only for qualifying mods) since Factorio's API is structured the same way, which is a natural fit. What it does

Magic chalk from chalk stone. Both magic chalk recipes, the flint one and the temporal one, take one chalk stone where they took one bone. The recipe tooltip names chalk stone.

Dark grimoires from rendered fat. Dark grimoires take rendered fat where they took raw fat, in the same amounts at each tier: 3, 6 and 9.

Installing

Known limits. Built against Rustbound Magic 3.2.5. It has not been run against the 4.x releases; if their recipes differ, this mod will refuse to load with an error rather than half-apply. Only the chalk and dark grimoire recipes are changed.

Bug reports go in the comments on this page. Requires Rustbound Magic, which is not included.

1	/**
2	 * Bulk-import the real Modrinth catalogue into `GameMod` — the "genuine
3	 * scale" pass NxLabs never had. Separate from `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`,
4	 * which stays the per-mod re-verification/freshness-check tool for rows that
5	 * already exist (this script creates/updates rows in the first place; run
6	 * verify-gamemods.ts afterward on a schedule to keep them fresh and to
7	 * backfill fileBytes/impact/dependencyCount, which this script deliberately
8	 * does not touch — see "WHAT THIS DOES NOT FETCH" below).
9	 *
10	 * WHY THIS EXISTS. As of 2026-09-19 NxLabs has 119 real (of 124 seeded)
11	 * hand-picked mod rows across 5 families. Modrinth alone publishes ~158k real
12	 * projects. This script queries Modrinth's actual public search API, filters
13	 * to content that is genuinely installable on a DEDICATED SERVER (Nxeon's
14	 * product), and upserts real rows — every field traces to a live API
15	 * response, nothing here is fabricated.
16	 *
17	 * SOURCE: Modrinth REST API v2, https://docs.modrinth.com/api/ — a fully
18	 * public, documented, third-party-integration-friendly API (the same one
19	 * `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts` already calls; this script reuses its request
20	 * pattern: identifying User-Agent, optional API key header, real 429/5xx
21	 * backoff, no attempt to mirror/rehost files — only metadata + hotlinked CDN
22	 * images, files are fetched by the worker at install time, same as today).
23	 *
24	 * PROJECT TYPES COVERED: mod, plugin, resourcepack, shader, datapack,
25	 * modpack. Deliberately EXCLUDED: `minecraft_java_server` (Modrinth's own
26	 * dedicated server-jar listing product — not installable "content" the way
27	 * the six above are).
28	 *
29	 * SERVER-RELEVANCE FILTER: Modrinth's `environment` facet says whether a
30	 * project runs client, server, or both. We only import environments that are
31	 * meaningfully server-side: server_only, dedicated_server_only,
32	 * server_only_client_optional, client_and_server, client_or_server,
33	 * client_or_server_prefers_both. We exclude client_only / singleplayer_only
34	 * on purpose — Nxeon hosts dedicated servers, not client mods.
35	 *   ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION: for project_type "plugin" we ALSO accept
36	 *   environment "unknown". Reason (checked live against the real API, not
37	 *   guessed): "plugin" on Modrinth structurally means Bukkit/Spigot/
38	 *   Paper/Sponge/Velocity server software — there is no such thing as a
39	 *   client-only plugin — but a large fraction of real, popular, genuinely
40	 *   server-only plugins simply never got the environment field filled in by
41	 *   their author (verified live: project_type:plugin + our environment list
42	 *   + downloads>1000 = 141 hits; the SAME query without the environment
43	 *   filter = 3340 hits, and manually sampling the gap showed real, popular,
44	 *   unambiguously server-side plugins like Chunky and Simple Voice Chat
45	 *   tagged "unknown"/"client_or_server_prefers_both"). Excluding "unknown"
46	 *   for plugins specifically would throw away real, relevant, high-quality
47	 *   catalogue content over a data-entry gap, not a real client/server
48	 *   distinction. Every other project type keeps the strict list, because for
49	 *   mods/resourcepacks/shaders/modpacks "unknown" genuinely can mean
50	 *   client-only.
51	 *
52	 * QUALITY THRESHOLD (script constants below, override with --min-downloads /
53	 * --min-follows): downloads > 1000 OR follows > 50. Implemented as two
54	 * disjoint search passes (Modrinth facets AND within a query; there is no
55	 * single-query OR across two different numeric fields) — pass 1 sorts by
56	 * downloads and takes everything over the download floor, pass 2 sorts by
57	 * follows and takes everything over the follow floor that pass 1 didn't
58	 * already take (`downloads<=floor`), so nothing is double-counted across
59	 * passes (cross-project-type duplicates from Modrinth's own
60	 * `all_project_types` overlap are still possible and handled by the
61	 * `seenProjectIds` set + the `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` upsert either
62	 * way).
63	 *
64	 * WHAT THIS DOES NOT FETCH (by design, to keep this a fast, few-thousand-
65	 * request bulk pass rather than a many-hour one): fileBytes,
66	 * dependencyCount, impact/impactNote. Those need a per-project `/version`
67	 * call each and are exactly what `verify-gamemods.ts` already does well —
68	 * re-run it with `--source=modrinth` after this script to backfill them, at
69	 * whatever pace is comfortable, on however many thousand rows this leaves it.
70	 *
71	 * EFFICIENCY: uses Modrinth's *bulk* endpoints so a page of 100 search hits
72	 * costs 3 requests total, not ~300: one `/v2/search` call, one
73	 * `/v2/projects?ids=[...]` call for the full record (clean `loaders` array
74	 * separate from tags, real `license` object, full `gallery` with
75	 * featured/ordering metadata, `server_side`), and one `/v2/users?ids=[...]`
76	 * call for real author avatars (search hits already carry `author`/
77	 * `author_id` directly — no team-lookup round trip needed the way a
78	 * single-project verify does).
79	 *
80	 * RATE LIMIT: 300 req/min per Modrinth, same with or without the API key (the
81	 * key just avoids being rejected as an unidentified client — real
82	 * contact-bearing User-Agent sent regardless). This script paces itself under
83	 * that (see RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN) and retries 429s honoring `Retry-After`.
84	 *
85	 * IDEMPOTENT: every write is `db.gameMod.upsert` on the real
86	 * `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` constraint — re-running updates the same
87	 * rows, never duplicates.
88	 *
89	 * SAFETY: this is a bulk-WRITE script against a real database, so it goes
90	 * through the same NXEON_DB_TARGET confirmation every other writing script in
91	 * this repo uses (scripts/db-target-guard.ts) and defaults to a dry run.
92	 *
93	 *   Dry run (no writes), one type, tiny slice — the sane way to first try this:
94	 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts \
95	 *       --project-types=mod --max-pages=1
96	 *
97	 *   Real write, one type, tiny slice:
98	 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts \
99	 *       --project-types=mod --max-pages=1 --apply
100	 *

content.thinking:
I have enough convention understanding from modio and steamworkshop already, since those importers closely match what I need for Vintage Story. Now I'm planning to write the Vintage Story importer, mirroring import-modio-catalog.ts's structure with its REST API handling, rate limiting, counters, dry-run/apply modes, and db-target-guard.

The key structural difference is that the Vintage Story API returns all 8,684 mods in a single call with no pagination needed. I'll filter out client-only mods and apply a downloads threshold of 1000 to match the Modrinth/modio precedent, which yields 3,932 candidates. For each qualifying mod I need to fetch detail records to get the full description, tags, and URLs, though I still need to verify whether the API exposes an explicit license field.

For gameVersions, I can pull the tags from the latest release, since those represent supported game versions. I'll leave fileBytes null since it's not directly exposed and matches how other importers defer that field, and for author info I'll use mod.author as authorName with authorAvatarUrl null since the VS API doesn't expose avatars. For serverSide, I can derive it directly from the "side" field.

Since I'm filtering out client-only mods, everything I import has side "server" or "both" — both cases mean the mod must be installed on the server to function, so I'll map both to serverSide "required" rather than trying to force VS's model into Modrinth's optional-content concept.

Now let me check logo and screenshot fields on an actual mod that has them.

Since tags are a flat freeform list, I'll use the first tag as the category (falling back to "Mod"), take logofile as the direct CDN URL, and cap screenshots for galleryUrls similar to the GALLERY_CAP=8 convention. Now I'm ready to write the scripts/import-vintagestory-catalog.ts importer.

The VS API returns all mods in a single call rather than paginated pages, so I'll fetch once, filter by server-side content and quality floor, then loop through qualifying mods fetching details with rate limiting — similar to how the steamworkshop importer handles authors for a qualified batch. Since there's no documented rate limit, I'll be conservative (~60/min) with the same retry-backoff pattern, skip the "families" arg since this is single-family, and add --max-items and --min-downloads flags analogous to the modio importer's conventions.

content.content:
1. **Split `resolveDownloadUrl` into a sync half (`resolveDownloadUrlSync`) and the network half.**
   spigotmc/steam_workshop/mod_io/github/etc. never needed a network call to begin with (spigotmc builds
   its Spiget URL synchronously; everything else just returns `mod.url`) — only modrinth/thunderstore do.
   `resolveDownloadUrlSync` returns immediately for every source except those two, and returns
   `undefined` (meaning "needs a live call") for them.
2. **StoreBrowser's grid now calls `resolveDownloadUrlSync` (0 network calls) instead of
   `resolveDownloadUrl` (up to 24 concurrent network calls) for every page render.** For the
   Modrinth/Thunderstore rows it can't resolve synchronously, it renders the new `DownloadButton` client
   component instead of a plain `<a>` — a click-to-resolve button that calls a new server action
   (`resolveModDownloadAction`, `lib/actions-mods.ts`) which runs the exact same `resolveDownloadUrl`
   function, but only for the ONE mod actually clicked, only when it's clicked. The mod detail pages
   (`app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`)
   are untouched — they already only ever resolved one mod and keep doing exactly that.
3. **Added a 5-second timeout (`AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`) to both live fetch calls inside
   `resolveDownloadUrl`.** There was no timeout at all before — this bounds the worst case for the
   single-mod detail-page/click-resolve call path, which had no cap before this fix.
4. **Added the 3 composite indexes `EXPLAIN` showed were missing**, to `GameMod` in
   `prisma/schema.prisma`: `(featured DESC, downloads DESC, popularity DESC, name)`,
   `(downloads DESC, name)`, `(createdAt DESC)` — matching `queryCatalogMods`'s real `ORDER_BY` shapes.
   Verified the fix live WITHOUT touching production schema: created each index inside a Postgres
   transaction against real production data, ran `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, then rolled back (0 indexes left
   behind, confirmed by re-querying `pg_indexes` after). Real before/after, same production data:
   featured sort **69.6ms → 0.099ms**, downloads sort **62.3ms → 0.082ms**, minecraft-family featured
   sort **68.2ms → 0.112ms** — Seq Scan + top-N heapsort became an Index Scan in every case, the same
   technique the existing `upstreamUpdatedAt` index already proved (a plain index on the sort column is
   enough; Postgres still applies `active`/`upstreamOk` as a cheap Filter during the index scan, no
   partial/filtered index needed — which Prisma's schema DSL can't express anyway). This is real,
   additive, forward-looking hardening (safe at today's 46MB table size regardless) rather than the
   actual fix for the reported symptom, per the measurements above. **Not yet applied to any database**
   — `prisma db push` was NOT run against `nxeon` or `nxeon_staging`; the schema change ships with the
   next real deploy the same way every other schema change in this repo does.
5. **Cached `listCatalogFamilies` and `totalDownloadsFor`** with `unstable_cache` (10-minute revalidate)
   — both were already cheap (24-30ms) so this isn't the fix for the reported symptom either, but it
   removes real repeated DB round trips under concurrent traffic for two aggregates that only change via
   periodic backfill scripts, never a live user action.

**Real before/after (production data, this session, via `scripts/_tmp-resolve-download-perf*.ts`,
`scripts/_tmp-resolve-download-after.ts`, deleted after use per convention):**

| Page (default sort, page 1) | Before (`resolveDownloadUrl` in the grid) | After (`resolveDownloadUrlSync` in the grid) |
|---|---|---|
| Cross-game `/mods` (7 of 24 mods are Modrinth) | 2079ms | 0ms (7 deferred to click-resolve) |
| `/mods/games/minecraft` (22 of 24 mods are Modrinth) | 2183ms | 0ms (22 deferred to click-resolve) |
| `/mods/games/minecraft?sort=downloads` | 2073ms | 0ms (22 deferred to click-resolve) |

Direct `curl` against the live production server before this fix: `/mods` 2.56-4.03s,
`/mods/games/minecraft` 2.60-3.51s (3 requests each). **The code fix above was NOT deployed to
production this session** (this task's process intentionally stops short of running
`deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` — the owner deploys after review), so a live post-fix `curl`
number does not yet exist; the ~2.0-2.2s removed from the render's critical path is the measured,
verified reduction, not a projection.

**Files touched:** `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, `lib/actions-mods.ts`, `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx`,
`components/mods/ModCard.tsx`, `components/mods/DownloadButton.tsx` (new), `prisma/schema.prisma`.

content.thinking:
There's a bug in the Vintage Story importer: a unique constraint violation on (gameFamily, slug), where my collision-avoidance loop only tries 3 attempts, which seems insufficient or points to a real bug. There's also a "no 'mod' in response" error for "thedungeon" — possibly a 404 or missing mod detail, maybe caused by the mod being deleted between the list and detail fetch, or a urlalias mismatch. I want to look into this more closely.

With CONCURRENCY=5 running via Promise.all, individual item failures shouldn't halt the whole run since each async function wraps its DB write in its own try/catch — the "no mod in response" case just increments the failed counter and returns cleanly. But the "Unique constraint failed" error is odd: it should also be caught by that same try/catch around the create call and logged through my formatted "[db] failed to upsert" message, yet the log instead shows a raw Prisma stack trace, which suggests the error isn't being caught where I expect.

Actually since PrismaClientKnownRequestError bakes its verbose stack into `.message` itself, my catch handler probably is firing correctly — it's just that `summary.urlalias` was null in that call, producing the odd "failed to upsert null" line.

That means some entry in the batch genuinely has `urlalias: null` from the API, not "thedungeon" itself but a different mod in the same concurrent batch, and template literal string coercion turns JS null into the literal text "null".

This traces to two separate bugs: a null urlalias breaking the detail fetch URL and causing "mod missing" errors, versus a distinct issue where my slug-deduplication retry loop only tries 3 times before failing with a unique constraint violation.

But now I realize the real bug is a race condition: since batches run with concurrency 5 in parallel, two items could both check the `usedSlugs` set and compute the same candidate slug before either has actually added it, since the check-then-act pattern isn't synchronized.

If slug were null, Prisma's schema would likely throw a required-field validation error rather than a unique constraint failure, so that theory doesn't quite explain the error trace either. Given time constraints, I should just tally up the total failures and judge whether this is a minor, acceptable failure rate.

Good, still running without crashing. I'm seeing 37 occurrences of "[db] failed" already, though each failure likely spans multiple lines since Prisma's error message includes a multi-line code frame with file and line info, so the actual count of distinct failures may differ from raw line matches.

Grep counts lines, and since I print the failure log once per call, 37 matches likely means 37 real failures — and with "progress:" appearing only 3 times (every 100 items), we're around item 200-300 of 3932, putting the failure rate at a concerning 12-18%. That's way higher than expected and points to a systematic bug rather than noise, likely tied to the repeated "Unique constraint failed on (gameFamily, slug)" error — maybe duplicate urlaliases across distinct mods, or a race condition in concurrent slug assignment as I'd suspected earlier. I should kill the job, dig into the root cause, and fix it before restarting.

I'm reconsidering the race theory: with CONCURRENCY=5 and batches awaited sequentially, races should only occur within a single batch of 5, which would need near-identical urlaliases among those 5 mods — unlikely to explain a 15% failure rate. So maybe the actual bug is something else entirely, like duplicate modids showing up in the original eligible list rather than a slug collision race.

I'm also double-checking whether the earlier smoke test wrote any rows — but it ran without --apply, so it was dry-run only and shouldn't have touched the database, matching the "0 existing" log line. That rules out stale existing rows as the cause, so I'm circling back to whether genuinely distinct mods could share the same urlalias, or whether my usedSlugs set isn't accumulating the way I assumed.

Actually, the real suspect is a race condition: since I'm fetching 5 items concurrently with Promise.all, and each does an async rate-limited detail fetch before checking-and-setting usedSlugs, that check-then-act pattern isn't atomic — though this would only cause a collision if two concurrent items genuinely started with identical urlalias values. I'm now wondering if it's something simpler instead: maybe my eligible array, filtered by server relevance and download threshold, includes entries whose urlalias doesn't resolve correctly when queried against the mod detail API.

That redirect theory makes more sense — old or renamed mod aliases can redirect to a different mod's canonical page, so two distinct list entries could end up resolving to the same underlying urlalias and collide on creation. Rather than chase down the exact cause further given time constraints, I'll just make the de-duplication logic more robust so it handles this regardless of root cause.

...unless two entries in my eligible list share the same modid — duplicate rows in the source data itself. That would explain it, so let me check if the mods API returns duplicate modid entries before guessing further; given the time pressure, I should kill the running job, look for duplicate modids/urlaliases directly, and fix the real underlying issue rather than continuing to speculate.

This confirms the "internal" category really means required dependency or asset packs for another mod — things like flib, stdlib, and boblibrary as shared code libraries, or the Space Exploration and Krastorio2 asset packs needed by those overhaul mods.

My earlier "Finale" example was a poor, unrepresentative sample; these internal mods are genuinely popular (flib alone is the most-downloaded Factorio mod) and are load-bearing dependencies a customer would actually need. So excluding "internal" wholesale was wrong — though I'm weighing whether asset-only companion packs like "Space Exploration Graphics Part 4" should still be deprioritized in browsing, similar to how Modrinth doesn't filter out libraries like Fabric API just because they're dependencies.

Since "internal" doesn't cleanly separate junk from legitimate content, and the codebase principle is to avoid inventing filters without clear justification, the more honest fix is to drop the category exclusion entirely and rely on the download-count threshold alone for quality control. I'm removing the internal-category filter now.

`node_modules`, own `.env`) so as not to touch the concurrent mod-description-pipeline agent's worktree.
Not deployed/pushed — the owner promotes after review, same convention as every other change in this file.

**New sources added:**
1. **`scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts`** — 10 new appids added to `FAMILY_APPID` (config only,
   internals untouched): gmod=4000, spaceengineers=244850, barotrauma=602960, terraria=1281930,
   stationeers=544550, kf2=232090, necesse=1169040, conan=440900, cs2=730, dayz=221100. Every appid is
   the game's real CLIENT Steam id, confirmed live via `IPublishedFileService/QueryFiles` (not the
   dedicated-server tool appid, which returns `total:0` for every family checked). Full `--apply` run:
   **9,521 new rows** (gmod/spaceengineers/barotrauma/terraria/stationeers/kf2/conan/cs2/dayz capped at
   the existing `maxPerFamily=1000` default; necesse's real pool is only 547, 521 cleared the
   `subscriptions>=25` floor).
2. **`scripts/import-vintagestory-catalog.ts`** (new) — Vintage Story ModDB (`mods.vintagestory.at/api`,
   MIT-licensed, keyless). Filters on the real author-set `side` field (excludes `client`-only, 868 of
   8,684), floor `downloads>1000`. **3,932 mods processed, 3,369 created.** Found and fixed live during
   the real run: ~40% of mods (3,471 of 8,684) have `urlalias: null` — the importer now fetches detail by
   the always-present numeric `modid` instead, with slug falling back to `modidstrs[0]` then `mod-{id}`,
   and `url` left honestly `null` (not fabricated) when no public alias page exists.
3. **`scripts/import-factorio-catalog.ts`** (new) — Factorio Mod Portal (`mods.factorio.com/api`,
   keyless). Metadata/listing only, per the task's own instruction — mod downloads need the customer's
   own factorio.com token, so no download URL is ever stored. Floor `downloads_count>1000`.
   **5,446 mods processed, 4,096 created.** Found and reversed live during the real run: an initial
   `category!=="internal"` filter (based on one sampled joke/tooling mod) would have silently excluded
   `flib` — the single most-downloaded mod on the entire portal (1,068,077) — plus `stdlib`, `boblibrary`
   and the required asset/graphics packs for popular overhaul mods (Space Exploration, Krastorio2); the
   filter was removed entirely, `internal` now displays as the honest, friendlier "Library / Dependency".
4. **`scripts/import-modio-catalog.ts`** — added Eco (mod.io game id 6, its real platform; Eco's own
   in-game Workshop is empty). **159 new rows** (floor `downloads_total>1000`, 592 real mods checked).

- **CS 1.6 (`cs16`), new, 9 entries** — CS 1.6 predates Steam Workshop (`appid 10` confirmed
  `total:0` live) and its community plugin forum (forums.alliedmods.net) blocks automated access

  server instead: AMX Mod X, ReHLDS, ReGameDLL_CS, ReAPI, ReUnion, ReVoice, PluginyCS BasePack,
  ReDeathmatch, Zombie Escape. Small and honest, not padded.
- **Minecraft: Noisium + ScalableLux** added (real Modrinth slugs, verified live) — were genuinely
  missing.
- Audit claimed Rust's GatherManager/StackSizeController were "missing from seed" — checked
  `prisma/seed-gamemods.ts`: both have been present since the 2026-08-15 seed commit. Audit was wrong
  on this point; no action taken. BetterNetworking_Valheim was checked too: `featured: false` already
  (never was flagged as a recommended mod), so "stop featuring" had nothing to do — left as-is.

**Checked and deliberately NOT adopted (ToS/reality judgment calls):**
- **CurseForge** — skipped. Live ToS check confirmed the audit: 3rd-party API terms explicitly forbid
  caching API data AND building anything that competes with CurseForge (which shipped its own hosting
  product with Shockbyte 2026-09-08). Real risk, no import.
- **ficsit.app (Satisfactory)** — skipped. Live ToS check: "may not be used in any application that is
  closed-source" — Nxeon's codebase is closed-source. No import.
- **Arma Reforger** — checked live, not assumed: its real mod platform is Bohemia's own Workshop
  (reforger.armaplatform.com/workshop), confirmed NOT Steam Workshop (`appid 1874880` → 1 Workshop item
  total). A different, undocumented API this importer doesn't speak — not built this pass.
- **ETS2 / ATS** — checked live: both DO have large real Steam Workshop pools (31,460 / 13,663 items),

  host's own client via the in-game `export_server_packages` console command into
  `server_packages.dat/.sii`, not fetched by the dedicated server from any catalog. No real
  "this installs on the server" claim exists here, so nothing was built rather than forcing one.

**Zero-mod gap, re-verified live against `nxeon_staging` (not prod, which already carries the original
10-family Steam Workshop pool):** of the games the task listed as selling with zero mods, this session's
new sources close **terraria, factorio, gmod, conan, vintagestory, necesse, kf2, barotrauma, stationeers,

task's scope, belongs to the concurrent mod-description-pipeline work), **enshrouded, theforest,

content.text:
## Summary

I researched and shipped real mod-data supplier expansion for Nxeon's NxLabs catalog, working entirely in an isolated worktree at **`/opt/nxeon-staging-moddata`** (branch `feature/mod-data-suppliers`, own `node_modules`, own `.env`) against **`nxeon_staging`** — never touched `/opt/nxeon` or prod, never committed or pushed (this repo auto-pushes `main` on every commit, so everything is left as uncommitted working-tree changes for the owner to review).

**Real numbers, verified live, applied to `nxeon_staging`:** 19,073 new `GameMod` rows (staging went from ~2,979 → 22,052 total).

| Source | What | New rows |
|---|---|---|
| Steam Workshop (10 new appids added to existing importer's config) | gmod, spaceengineers, barotrauma, terraria, stationeers, kf2, necesse, conan, cs2, dayz | 9,521 |
| Factorio Mod Portal (new importer) | metadata/listing only, no downloads proxied | 4,096 |
| Vintage Story ModDB (new importer) | filtered on real `side` field | 3,369 |
| mod.io (Eco added to existing importer) | | 159 |
| Hand-seeded (CS 1.6 + Minecraft) | AMX Mod X/ReHLDS stack, Noisium, ScalableLux | 11 |

**Two real bugs found and fixed mid-run** (not shipped broken): Vintage Story's list API has `urlalias: null` on ~40% of mods — fixed by fetching detail via the always-present numeric `modid`. Factorio's `category:"internal"` filter would have silently excluded **flib**, the single most-downloaded mod on the whole portal, plus other real shared libraries — filter removed entirely after checking live data disproved the assumption.

**Judgment calls, all with live-verified reasoning (documented in code comments and `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`):**
- Skipped **CurseForge** and **ficsit.app** — live ToS checks confirmed real risk (CurseForge bans caching + competing products; ficsit.app bans closed-source apps).
- **Arma Reforger** has no real Steam Workshop presence (1 item) — its actual platform is Bohemia's own Workshop, a different undocumented API, not built this pass.
- **ETS2/ATS** have huge Steam Workshop pools but no server-side install mechanism (mods are client-exported via `export_server_packages`) — said so rather than forcing a fake importer.
- Audit's claim that Rust's GatherManager/StackSizeController were "missing from seed" was **wrong** — both were already in `prisma/seed-gamemods.ts` since 2026-08-15; no action taken there.
- Zero-mod gap closed for **10 of ~21** listed games (terraria, factorio, gmod, conan, vintagestory, necesse, kf2, barotrauma, stationeers, eco); **11 remain genuinely zero** with documented reasons (3 are ToS/scope calls, 8 have no viable source among the 4 requested suppliers).

**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; full test suite unchanged at 1385/1422 (confirmed the 37 failures are pre-existing/unrelated by stashing my changes and re-running against the same baseline).

Files: `scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts`, `scripts/import-modio-catalog.ts` (edited), `scripts/import-vintagestory-catalog.ts`, `scripts/import-factorio-catalog.ts` (new), `prisma/seed-gamemods.ts`, `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma` (comment), `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` — all in `/opt/nxeon-staging-moddata`.

result: Added 19,073 real, live-verified mods to nxeon_staging via 2 new importers (Vintage Story ModDB, Factorio Mod Portal) + Steam Workshop/mod.io config expansion + hand-seeded CS16, closing the zero-mod gap for 10 games while honestly documenting 11 that remain unclosed and 2 ToS-risk sources deliberately skipped; typecheck clean, no test regressions, nothing pushed or deployed.
